clue.text: Drunk son serving wine bottles

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the serving contains the son

parts.note: a plate is a serving of food, as in a plate of stew
red is a colour of wine, so wine gives red

explanation.surface: A son who waits at table is the worse for drink while the wine bottles stand around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun for the wine but is the verb that puts S inside PLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastered is informal slang for heavily intoxicated, a synonym of drunk.

clue.text: Submit shortly after sex

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its final letter, here from the word for after

parts.note: post- means after, as in postwar
it is a coy word for sex, as in 'doing it'

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about submitting soon after sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' is not time here: it trims the last letter of POST, leaving POS.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward an idea for consideration, which is what submitting an argument means.

clue.text: While embracing model escort is in danger

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold around, so the word for while goes around the car letter

parts.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'
the Model T was the famous Ford car, so model gives T
to escort someone is to take them somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone hugging a model while working as an escort is putting themselves in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at stake is at risk of being lost, which is being in danger.

clue.text: Mouth of river feeding water supply

indicators.note: feeding into something means going inside it, so the river letter goes into the tap

parts.note: a tap supplies water

explanation.surface: A river's mouth feeds a water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth of river' reads as one phrase, but 'Mouth' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.

clue.text: Buzz Aldrin not half getting acceleration due to gravity

indicators.note: losing half of the astronaut's surname leaves its last three letters

parts.note: g is the physics symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: The astronaut Buzz Aldrin, half-gone, feeling the pull of gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz Aldrin' looks like a name, but Buzz is the definition and Aldrin the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a buzz or a ring are both informal ways of saying a phone call.

clue.text: Slip into supermarket for reduction: avoid one with bill

parts.note: to don clothes is to slip into them

indicators.note: reducing the shop's name cuts its final letter

parts.note: Aldi is a discount supermarket chain
to duck a question is to avoid it

explanation.surface: Nipping into the supermarket for a cut-price deal while dodging someone who wants payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' reads as an invoice, but it is a beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney cartoon duck has a beak, a bill, so he is one with a bill.

clue.text: Man entering pub's rejected treatment

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the whole is read backwards
the pronoun goes inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub; the 's stands for 'is'
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man walking into a pub that has refused him treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is a course of treatment for addiction, short for rehabilitation.

clue.text: Guy, large one having scales go up on this?

parts.note: a guy is a rope holding a tent steady
L is the clothing abbreviation for large
an adder is a snake, which has scales

explanation.surface: A big scaly creature climbing up something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' suggests climbing, but it means a snake's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder made of rope is something climbers or sailors climb, so you go up on it.

clue.text: With cases of holiday diarrhoea, tandoori ultimately contained tapeworm larva

indicators.note: the cases of words are their outside letters, first and last of each
ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A holiday tummy bug after a curry turns out to be a tapeworm.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydatid is a cyst formed by the larval stage of certain tapeworms.

clue.text: Sell-by date's close: US shifting targets

indicators.note: shifting letters moves them around into a new order
a word's close is its final letter, here of date

explanation.surface: A sell-by date running out and America moving its targets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges SELLBY, E (the close of 'date') and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullseyes are the centres of dartboards and archery boards, the things you aim at.

clue.text: Hit ten? Dua Lipa sings part on piano

indicators.note: letters that are hit are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Pop star Dua Lipa singing her tenth hit, accompanied on piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' looks like a chart record, but it signals the anagram of TEN, DUA LIPA and SINGS; Dua Lipa is a British pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sustaining pedal is the pedal of a piano that lets the notes ring on.

clue.text: Half of inked design around middle of her nipple

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second
halving the word for the inked design keeps its first three letters

parts.note: a tattoo is a design inked into skin

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word her

explanation.surface: Half a tattoo circles her nipple.
explanation.definitionFit: A teat is the nipple of a breast or udder, or of a baby's bottle.

clue.text: Shout was one of hers coming back: worried, heading to scary howls

indicators.note: the singer's name comes back, read backwards

parts.note: 'Shout' was a 1964 hit for the Scottish singer Lulu
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A singer recalls her old hit, anxious ahead of a scary howling crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To ululate is to wail or howl, a long trilling cry.

clue.text: Join masses dancing for music performance

indicators.note: letters that dance move around into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to join the crowds dancing at a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam session is an informal, improvised gathering of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Poor English grade after that subject is not taught

indicators.note: the English and grade pieces come after the subject

parts.note: ill can mean poor, as in ill health
IT, information technology, is a school subject
a rate is a grade or class, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A poor English mark is put down to a subject never being taught.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone illiterate cannot read or write, having never been taught to.

clue.text: Got it: Prince, with reference to Virginia, lied terribly

parts.note: re means regarding, with reference to
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: something done terribly is messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prince lied terribly about Virginia, and the listener saw through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got it' looks like understanding, but means won the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win through, so prevailed means triumphed or came out on top.

clue.text: Supplier protecting this writer, following book launch, primarily

definitions.text: Supplier protecting this writer, following book launch, primarily

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the supplier goes around the rest

parts.note: a pusher supplies drugs

indicators.note: the writer's pronoun follows the book letters
primarily picks the first letter of launch

parts.note: this writer is the setter, who would say I

explanation.surface: A firm that supplies books, guarding its author after a launch.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that issues books supplies them to the public and looks after its authors after a launch.

clue.text: Suspect Harry is holding back in Scotland Yard

indicators.note: the pursuit word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: to harry someone is to dog them, pursue relentlessly

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A suspect named Harry is held at the Metropolitan Police headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotland Yard' is the London police headquarters, but splits here into the last letter of Scotland and Y for yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgy is informal British for suspect or untrustworthy.

clue.text: Resists American money

definitions.meaning: ..., as in '... the trend', means resists or opposes

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to pay in US dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is slang for a dollar, and to buck is to go against something.

clue.text: Gets into a ball with corkscrew and drink

parts.note: a corkscrew is a spiral, a curl
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Getting the party going with a corkscrew and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance, but it means a round shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To curl up is to roll yourself into a round shape, like a cat sleeping.

clue.text: Appreciates marks on wicket, batting first

indicators.note: the batting word comes first

parts.note: a batter is 'in' while batting in cricket
creases are the lines marked on a cricket pitch by the wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket line about the marks on the pitch when batting first.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the creases are white lines painted at each end of the pitch; a batter at the crease is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing that appreciates rises in value, so it grows larger.

clue.text: Field for guinea pig?

definitions.meaning: a field of study, such as history
a person tested on in an experiment; the question mark says it is a figure of speech

explanation.surface: A field for a guinea pig to run in.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject is both an area of study and a person used in an experiment.

clue.text: Floods where Moses was found

definitions.meaning: a flood is a rush of water pouring in
the baby Moses was found in a basket among the bulrushes

explanation.surface: Floods at the place where the baby Moses was found.
explanation.definitionFit: Inrushes are sudden incoming surges, like floods; read as two words, it is the place among the reeds.

clue.text: Early victim of some Bible-basher turned back

indicators.note: the letters taken are read backwards
some of the phrase means a few of its letters, run together

explanation.surface: A Bible-thumping preacher turns back to talk about the first murder victim.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Cain's brother is the first person to be murdered, an early victim.

clue.text: No-hoper is more relaxed with one round to go

indicators.note: a piece to go is to be taken away

parts.note: looser means more relaxed
O is a round letter

explanation.surface: A boxer with no hope, more relaxed with one round left.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone certain to fail, the person who always comes off worst.

clue.text: Droppings from small animal

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: Droppings left by a small animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is the naturalist's word for animal dung.

clue.text: Live on a field

indicators.note: the a comes on after the first piece

parts.note: are is a form of the verb 'to be', meaning to exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone living on a farm field.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a field of study or activity, as in an area of expertise.

clue.text: Hotel's crap iron's rubbish for folds …

indicators.note: something rubbish is wrecked, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A guest complains the hotel's iron is too poor to press the bedsheets.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital corners are the neat tucked folds of a sheet at the end of a made bed.

clue.text: … iron, not working over fold, to turn red, perhaps?

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters left are read backwards
on can mean working, so removing on leaves the rest of the word

parts.note: a fold and a pen are both enclosures for sheep

explanation.surface: An iron left switched off over a fold, going red.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit such as a tomato turns red as it matures, so ripening is one example of turning red.

clue.text: Another to court men one takes out

parts.note: an extra is one more, another
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers, the men

explanation.surface: Another suitor courting a man, hoping to take one out on a date.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor removes things, such as a fan pulling out smells or a dental tool.
